GENERATED DOCUMENT -- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Produced by `npx tsx scripts/generate-openapi.ts` from the /v1 route sources: paths and methods from the route files on disk, scopes from each route's requireApiKey() call, request bodies from the zod schemas the routes parse with, responses from the return types of the `serialize*` functions they call, and error codes from STATUS_BY_CODE. Where a route validates its body with hand-written checks instead of a zod schema, this document says so on the operation rather than guessing a field list.

MONEY AND UNITS. Every monetary field on this API is a whole number of DOLLARS, never cents: $10,378.00 is 10378. Amounts below one dollar are not representable and are refused rather than rounded. The one column stored in cents is `BankTransaction.amount`, and the read path converts it, so `GET /v1/bank-link/{id}/transactions` publishes dollars like every other endpoint. Rates are percentages: 11.8 means 11.8 %.

requestBody.description: Field NAMES are derived from the route's ACCEPTED_PARAMS guard and are exact; any other key is a 400. Per-field types are enforced by hand-written checks and are not derivable, so none is published here.

x-refused-parameters.email: 'email' is not accepted: the applicant id is DERIVED from the lowercased email (apl_ + a hash of your organization id and that address), so changing it would change the id in the URL of this very request. It would not rename the applicant either — cases that cannot be rewritten keep the old address, leaving one person split across two ids with partial history under each. To onboard a corrected address, submit an application under it with POST /v1/underwrite.
x-refused-parameters.applicant_email: 'applicant_email' is not accepted; see 'email', which is not accepted either: the applicant id is derived from the email address.
x-refused-parameters.status: 'status' is not accepted: it is DERIVED, not stored. An applicant is 'active' when any of their cases was updated in the last 90 days and 'inactive' otherwise, and there is no column to set. Updating a case's contact details is itself activity.
x-refused-parameters.type: 'type' is not accepted: the applicant type (individual or business) is an UNDERWRITING INPUT — it selects the rules an application is analyzed under — not a contact detail. Changing it on an analyzed case would mean the decision was made under rules the record no longer claims.
x-refused-parameters.applicant_type: 'applicant_type' is not accepted; the parameter is named 'type', and it is not accepted either: the applicant type is an underwriting input, not a contact detail.
x-refused-parameters.credit_score: 'credit_score' is not accepted: it is read from the bureau report on the applicant's most recent case carrying one. Nothing may assert a score.
x-refused-parameters.total_applications: 'total_applications' is not accepted: it is a count of the applicant's cases.
x-refused-parameters.active_loans: 'active_loans' is not accepted: it is a count of the applicant's open loans.
x-refused-parameters.total_borrowed: 'total_borrowed' is not accepted: it is a sum over the applicant's originated loans.
x-refused-parameters.assigned_to: 'assigned_to' is not accepted: an underwriter is assigned to a CASE, not to an applicant. This endpoint does not address individual cases.
x-refused-parameters.assignedTo: 'assignedTo' is not accepted: an underwriter is assigned to a CASE, not to an applicant.
x-refused-parameters.id: 'id' is not accepted: the applicant is taken from the URL path, and the id is derived rather than assigned.
x-refused-parameters.applicant_id: 'applicant_id' is not accepted: the applicant is taken from the URL path.
x-refused-parameters.case_id: 'case_id' is not accepted: this endpoint updates the applicant, which is every one of their cases that can still be changed. To address one case, use the case endpoints.
x-refused-parameters.idempotency_key: 'idempotency_key' is not accepted as a body field: send it as the 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header.

decision.description: approve, decline or review; the past-tense spellings are aliases. Matched case-insensitively.

conditions.description: Only with `approve`. Each is stored as a required prior-to-funding condition.

get.summary: the files attached to one case, paginated.

post.summary: attach a file to a case. Multipart, with one `file` part of at most 25 MiB (26,214,400 bytes) plus the string fields below. De-duplication is by content hash and is PER CASE: the same bytes uploaded twice to one case are refused with 409 `conflict`, and `details.existing_document_id` names the copy. The same bytes on a DIFFERENT case in your organization are accepted — a voided check, an ID scan or a signed application legitimately belongs on more than one case for the same merchant. Nothing is written on the refused path. A `financial` document also starts an analysis of the case; several of them queue one run, not one each.

parameters.description: Replays the first response for a repeated request. Reusing a key with a different body is `idempotency_key_reused` (409), never a silent replay.

category.description: Defaults to `other`. Matched case-insensitively; the label spelling ("ID Verification") is accepted too.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the uploaded filename.

description.description: Alias of `name`, read only when `name` is absent.

apiKey.description: API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Every operation additionally requires a scope from its `x-required-scopes`, which is what the route passes to `requireApiKey`. Where that list has more than one entry, ANY ONE of them authorizes the call — they are alternatives, not requirements. Scopes are not expressed in `security` because OpenAPI only carries scopes for oauth2 and openIdConnect schemes. Key scope vocabulary: products:read, underwrite:write, cases:read, cases:write, cases:decide, bank_link:write, documents:read, documents:write, portfolio:read, portfolio:write, collections:read, collections:write, applicants:read, applicants:write, webhooks:manage, branding:manage, decisions:read, decisions:write, decision_policies:manage.

remaining_principal.description:
Whole dollars: the contractual principal still outstanding after this
installment is paid as scheduled. It moves with the schedule, not with
money received, so it differs from `current_balance` on the loan whenever
an installment is paid late, short or not at all.

kind.description: `analyze` for the run queued at submission, `reanalyze` for a re-run.

already_queued.description:
True when this call did NOT queue new work because a run was already
pending or in flight, and the job below is that existing run. Re-running a
case that is already queued is a no-op, not a second run — otherwise a
partner polling and retrying would stack duplicate analyses of one case.

SerializedAnalysisJob.description:
A queued analysis, as `POST /v1/cases/{id}/reanalyze` returns it.

Deliberately thin. `ApplicationJob` also carries `attempts`, `maxAttempts`,
`lockedBy`, `lockedAt`, `nextAttemptAt` and `lastError` — a worker lease and a
stack trace. None of that is a partner's business: `lockedBy` names internal
infrastructure and `lastError` is an unbounded upstream message that may quote
applicant data back. A partner needs to know the run was accepted and how to
follow it, which is the case id and the job's own state.

SerializedApplicantUpdate.description:
The `PATCH /v1/applicants/:id` response: the applicant as they now stand,
PLUS what the fan-out actually did.

THE TWO COUNTS ARE THE POINT. An applicant is N cases, and this endpoint
writes only the ones that carry no underwriting decision, no originated
loan and no pulled credit or background evidence — the rest are left exactly
as the decision was made on them. A response that reported only the new
contact details would be true and still misleading: a partner correcting a
phone number across an applicant with eight decided cases and one live one
has changed one row, and needs to be able to see that.

`cases_preserved` is deliberately not called "skipped" or "failed". Nothing
failed; those rows were protected, which is the behaviour, not a shortfall.

accounts.description: 1 when a bank account is connected, otherwise 0. A case holds at most one linked account.

current_balance.description: Null when no balance was measured. Never estimated, never zero-filled.

lowest_balance_30d.description:
ALWAYS NULL. The platform does not compute a 30-day minimum balance and
never publishes an estimate in its place.

amount.description: Whole dollars, like every amount on this API.

status.description: `pending` until every item has terminated, then `completed`. There is no intermediate value.

total.description: Items submitted. Immutable: a batch never grows.

failed.description: Terminated in failure — at creation, or after the analysis gave up.

completed_at.description: Null until the batch completes; set once, by the fence that emits the event.

applications.description:
PER-ITEM OUTCOMES, not just a count. A batch that reported only totals
could say "12 submitted, 3 failed" and leave a partner to diff their own
request against `GET /v1/cases` to discover WHICH three — which defeats the
purpose of handing back a batch id instead of 50 case ids.

case_id.description:
Null ONLY for an item that never reached a case — i.e. one that failed at
creation. A `pending` or `succeeded` item always has one.

error.description: A short sentence saying why the item failed, or null. Never a stack trace.

SerializedBatchItem.description:
ONE submitted application's outcome within a batch.

`index` IS THE PARTNER'S HANDLE. They sent an ordered array; this is how a
result is matched back to the element that produced it. It is not decorative
— without it a partner holding 50 case ids and 50 submissions has no way to
pair them except by guessing from applicant names, which are not unique.

decision.description:
The recorded outcome, or null. Null is the review case: a review records
no outcome, and `status` (`review`) is the whole answer.

decided_by.description: `api_key:<key id>` — the API key that recorded the decision.

approved_amount.description: Whole dollars. Null when the decision carries no approved amount.

conditions.description: Echoed back only when the caller sent conditions; [] otherwise.

processing.description:
Where the application is right now, in plain words — read this, not a
stage you stored at submission time. `message` is written to be shown to a
person as-is; `next_step` says who must act (`upload_statements`, `wait`,
`retry`, `decide`, `none`). Absent only if progress could not be loaded.

assessment.description:
Document integrity, evidence sufficiency and creditworthiness, kept apart:
a decline for forged statements is not a finding that the borrower cannot
repay. Absent only if it could not be computed.

amount.description: Null when the submission named no amount. See `SerializedUnderwriteSubmission.amount`.

risk_score.description:
The risk score, or null when no analysis has run. Null is never a score:
a measured 0, the best possible score, is published as 0.

risk_level.description: Null when no analysis has run — in exactly the cases `risk_score` is null.

run_number.description:
Null when no analysis has run. Treat it as the presence signal for the
whole `ai_analysis` block: `risk_score` and `risk_level` are null exactly
when it is.

status.description: `obtained` when a credit report is on file; `not_obtained` otherwise.

score.description: The bureau score, or null when no credit report is on file.

deposit_breakdown.description:
Deposits sorted into revenue, wages, transfers, loan proceeds, refunds,
cash and unclassified, with qualifying monthly revenue (dollars). Null
when the statements were not classified.

source.description:
How the bank evidence arrived: `plaid` (open banking), `statements`
(uploaded and read by the platform), `manual`, or null when there is
none. `connected` is true only for `plaid`. A partner that reads
`connected: false` as "no bank evidence" shows a reviewer "No bank
connected" over a case built on three months of statements — this field
is what lets them tell the two apart.

deposit_trend_pct.description:
Statement path only; null / 0 for a Plaid link. `deposit_trend_pct` is the
% change in monthly deposits from the first statement read to the last.
`stacked_lenders` counts distinct lenders with recurring debits — 2 or
more means the applicant is already servicing multiple advances.

total_balance.description:
NULL when the platform holds no measured balance for the account —
because the provider returned none, or because no bank was ever linked.
NEVER estimated, and never zero-filled: a $0 balance is a measurement
("this account is empty") and absence is not.

lowest_balance_30d.description:
ALWAYS NULL. The platform does not compute a 30-day minimum balance and
never publishes an estimate in its place.

nsf_events_90d.description: Non-sufficient-funds events in the trailing 90 days — the window the data covers.

message.description: One or two plain sentences: what is happening and what, if anything, to do.

next_step.description: Who must act: `upload_statements` (you), `wait` (HL Hunt is working), `retry` (HL Hunt hit a problem — POST /reanalyze), `decide` (the lender), `none`.

reason.description: Why it is waiting or failed: `no_statements`, `statements_unreadable`, `processing_error`; null otherwise.

last_attempt_at.description: When HL Hunt last worked on it (ISO 8601), or null if it never has.

in_progress.description: True while HL Hunt is actively queued or analysing.

Where an application is right now, written to be shown to a person as-is.
Returned on `GET /v1/cases`, `GET /v1/cases/{id}` and the
`application.analysis_failed` webhook. Built by `describeCaseProgress`.

new_balance.description: Whole dollars: the loan's remaining balance after this payment was applied.

SerializedSendLink.description:
The one shape `POST /v1/applicants/:id/send-link` returns for BOTH link
types. `link_type` echoes the discriminator the partner sent.

pipeline_stage.description:
Where the case is in the underwriting pipeline, as distinct from `status`,
which is the DECISION. One of:

- `queued` — accepted, waiting for the analysis to run.
- `awaiting_documents` — you declared `bank_verification: "statements"`, so
  nothing is queued until you upload them. Upload a `financial` document
  and the analysis starts.
- `awaiting_evidence` — the analysis ran and found nothing to read: no
  credit report, no bank data, no background check. Not a failure; the case
  is waiting for evidence. Uploading a `financial` document starts a fresh
  run on its own.
- `analyzed` — an analysis completed. `status` carries the outcome.
- `failed` — the analysis could not complete for a reason on our side.
  `POST /v1/cases/{id}/reanalyze` retries it.

amount.description:
Whole dollars: the amount requested, exactly as submitted.

NULL when the submission named no amount at all — which is a different
thing from 0, and is what a platform sends when it wants the analysis to
size the deal. Never substitute 0 here: the prompts and the auto-approve
rules both read 0 as a real figure.

bank_link_url.description:
Present only when the request sent `bank_link: true`; absent means no link
was requested. `null`, with `bank_link_status` `"failed"`, when the link
could not be created — the application is still accepted, and a link can be
minted later with POST /v1/bank-link.

bank_link_status.description:
Present only when the request sent `bank_link: true`. `"ready"` when
`bank_link_url` carries a link; `"failed"` when it is `null`.

bank_link_id.description:
The link's id, for `GET /v1/bank-link/{id}/status` and
`/transactions`. Present whenever `bank_link_url` is; `null` when the
link could not be created.

Without this a link minted at submit was unpollable: the id existed, and
the response dropped it. `POST /v1/bank-link` returned one, this did not,
so the same resource was addressable or not depending on which door it
came through.

bank_link_expires_at.description:
When the link stops working, so a partner forwarding it to an applicant
knows how long they have. `null` when the link could not be created, and
also when it carries no expiry.

events.description: The event types this endpoint is subscribed to.

products.description:
Product slugs this endpoint is limited to. EMPTY means every product,
which is the default — an endpoint that named no products hears about all
of them, exactly as every endpoint did before this filter existed.

mode.description: `live` or `test` — the mode of the API key that registered it.
